mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Discovery P300 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Land Rover Discovery P300 typically ranges from £4,200 to £6,500 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £1,500 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing 204PT engine in a Land Rover Discovery P300?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Land Rover Discovery P300 are unexplained coolant loss, a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts (timing chain rattle), or illuminated temperature warning lights. You should also check for sweet-smelling exhaust or oil residue around the valve cover.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Discovery P300?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A typical Land Rover Discovery P300 holds a UK market value of £25,000-£45,000, making a £4,200-£6,500 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment that preserves the vehicle's performance, reliability and strong resale value for years to come.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Discovery P300 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Discovery P300 typically takes 2 to 4 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Land Rover Discovery P300 and the D300 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Land Rover Discovery P300 uses a 2.0-litre turbocharged inline-4 petrol engine (204PT) producing 300 PS, prioritising smooth, responsive performance and refinement. In contrast, the D300 uses a 3.0-litre inline-6 mild-hybrid diesel engine focused on low-end torque and fuel economy for heavy towing.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Discovery P300 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the all-new L462 Land Rover Discovery 5 launched, the P300 badge introduced a refined, high-output 2.0-litre turbocharged Ingenium petrol engine, offering a smooth and responsive alternative to the diesel lineup for the premium 7-seat SUV.

milestones.description: Introduction of the 204PT / AJ200P 2.0L turbocharged inline-4 petrol engine (300 PS / 296 hp) in the Discovery 5, paired with an 8-speed ZF automatic and permanent four-wheel drive.
Present - Continued production with minor engine management software updates to improve throttle response and emissions compliance; the 2.0L Ingenium architecture remains unchanged.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Discovery P300 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 2.0-litre Ingenium petrol (204PT) in the Land Rover Discovery P300 is generally more reliable than its diesel Ingenium siblings, but cooling system wear and occasional timing chain stretch remain the dominant replacement drivers. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Water Pump & Cooling System Failure - Why the Land Rover Discovery P300 204PT Overheats
problems.rootCause: Plastic components in the cooling system (thermostat housing, water pump) can become brittle under sustained thermal cycling, leading to coolant leaks and subsequent overheating risks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, and hoses with upgraded metal/composite parts.
repairOptions.longevity: Extends life significantly if caught before overheating damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded cooling components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has already suffered thermal damage or warped heads.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Discovery P300 of relevant age (2017-present) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £25,000-£45,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader market observations]. At this premium value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement is a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and easily justifies the investment to preserve performance and resale value.
problems.recommendation: If your Land Rover Discovery P300 is exhibiting minor coolant seepage but has not suffered thermal damage, a targeted preventative cooling system refresh by a JLR specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has overheated, a full rebuilt replacement is the only reliable long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 204PT Land Rover Discovery P300 engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the Land Rover Discovery P300 204PT Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Over time, the timing chain tensioners can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch and produce a characteristic rattling noise on cold starts. If ignored, this can lead to catastrophic internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip front covers, replace timing chain, guides and updated tensioner assembly.
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive fix for chain rattle; prevents catastrophic valve-to-piston contact if addressed promptly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded valvetrain components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended only if chain failure has already caused internal engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, the £25,000-£45,000 value of a Land Rover Discovery P300 makes targeted repairs like a timing chain refresh highly viable. A full engine replacement is rarely justified for chain rattle alone unless secondary damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle in your Land Rover Discovery P300. A timely chain and tensioner replacement by a specialist is a well-documented fix that preserves the engine's longevity at a fraction of the cost of a full rebuild.
